tagline: Up through the pines to the rim above the desert.
intro: From Interstate 8 the Sunrise Highway starts up into the Laguna Mountains along a cliff above Pine Valley, still in chaparral and sagebrush, and the forest closes in as it climbs, pine and spruce and fir with meadows between. At Mount Laguna, a hamlet near 6,000 feet in the Jeffrey pines, it reaches the high point of the drive, then runs on north past overlooks into Anza-Borrego toward Highway 79.

The road was built in 1937, and the flat at the Pine Valley Overlook is the borrow pit its builders dug. The Pacific Crest Trail passes this way, and day hikers can reach it from the picnic areas along the road.

moments.title: Desert View Picnic Area
moments.text: Lunch here comes with the desert 6,000 feet below, and on most days the Salton Sea in plain sight to the southeast.

moments.title: El Prado Cabin
moments.text: In Laguna Campground just off the byway stands a one-room log cabin of 1912, for years the forest's only station, where one ranger saw to fire lookout, grazing permits and camping.

moments.title: Penny Pines
moments.text: A monument thanks the children and groups who collect pennies every year to plant trees in the forest, and a short walk behind it is the penny pine plantation itself.
